Past-tense overregularization

Source: R/data.R
overregularization.Rd

Overregularization errors (goed, holded) out of all irregular past-tense contexts, for 24 children recorded every six months from 30 to 60 months. The simulation follows the account of Marcus et al. (1992): errors are rare, their rate does not change with age, and children differ in how often they make them. Maratsos (2000) disputed the low rates, arguing that averages over all verbs hide much higher rates for verbs a child uses rarely and periods in which a child overregularizes often. These data have no verb-level information. For binomial models of errors out of attempts and for testing an effect that is absent.

Usage

overregularization

Format

A tibble with 144 rows and 4 columns:

child

Child ID, C01 to C24.

age

Age in months.

attempts

Irregular past-tense contexts in the recording.

errors

Overregularizations among them.

Source

data-raw/overregularization.R

Details

True model, in log-odds: -3.66, with by-child intercepts of SD 0.9, so the median child makes errors in 2.5% of attempts and a few children in many more. Age has no effect. Children attempt more irregular past tenses as they get older. Marcus et al. (1992) report a median rate of 2.5% and a mean of 4.2% across 25 children, with a roughly constant rate from age 2 into the school years. Maratsos (2000) showed that pooling all tokens gives most weight to frequent verbs, whose rates are lowest. The children and counts are simulated.

References

Marcus, G. F., Pinker, S., Ullman, M., Hollander, M., Rosen, T. J. & Xu, F. (1992). Overregularization in language acquisition. Monographs of the Society for Research in Child Development, 57(4). doi:10.2307/1166115

Maratsos, M. (2000). More overregularizations after all: New data and discussion on Marcus, Pinker, Ullman, Hollander, Rosen & Xu. Journal of Child Language, 27(1), 183-212. doi:10.1017/S0305000999004067

Examples

sum(overregularization$errors) / sum(overregularization$attempts)
#> [1] 0.03727715
aggregate(cbind(errors, attempts) ~ age, data = overregularization, FUN = sum)
#>   age errors attempts
#> 1  30     16      370
#> 2  36     18      503
#> 3  42     18      648
#> 4  48     31      796
#> 5  54     35      933
#> 6  60     43     1069
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::glmer(cbind(errors, attempts - errors) ~ I((age - 45) / 12) + (1 | child),
                   data = overregularization, family = binomial)
  summary(m)$coefficients
}
#>                     Estimate Std. Error     z value     Pr(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)      -3.48754528  0.1772913 -19.6712757 3.800969e-86
#> I((age - 45)/12)  0.03074469  0.1011252   0.3040259 7.611082e-01
